gloss: to reel in; to roll up; to wind up

definitions.gloss: to reel in; to roll up; to wind up
definitions.explanation: To wind something around a spool, reel, or similar device, gathering it up by rolling or winding. Used for thread, tape, film, fishing line, and similar materials.

examples.japanese: リールで{釣|つ}り{糸|いと}を{巻|ま}き{取|と}った。
examples.english: I reeled in the fishing line with the reel.

examples.japanese: {使|つか}い{終|お}わったホースを{巻|ま}き{取|と}って{片付|かたづ}けた。
examples.english: I rolled up the hose after using it and put it away.

notes:
A compound verb formed from {巻|ま}く (to wind, to roll) + {取|と}る (to take). The {取|と}る component adds the sense of gathering or collecting the wound material.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {糸|いと}を{巻|ま}き{取|と}る: to wind up thread
- テープを{巻|ま}き{取|と}る: to wind up tape
- ホースを{巻|ま}き{取|と}る: to roll up a hose
- {釣|つ}り{糸|いと}を{巻|ま}き{取|と}る: to reel in fishing line
- フィルムを{巻|ま}き{取|と}る: to wind up film

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {巻|ま}く: to wind, to roll — the base verb; broader usage including wrapping around something
- {巻|ま}き{上|あ}げる: to roll up, to hoist — emphasizes upward motion; also means to swindle (colloquial)
- {手繰|たぐ}る: to pull in hand over hand — pulling rope or line toward oneself without winding

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive verb. Takes を for the object being wound up.
